# Jevyr advisory action

This composite action binds a one-shot Jevyr case to an exact full Git SHA, watches the live event stream to termination, exports the signed Seal, Record, and terminal closure with the complete replay-verified ledger, and verifies that subject and runtime source remain unchanged afterward. `subject-directory` identifies the separately checked-out repository under judgment; for a pull request, the companion `pull_request_target` workflow loads executable Jevyr code, policy, ignore rules, and the Assay Frontier from the exact base commit, never from the synthetic merge ref or pull-request checkout. The proposed change therefore supplies frozen subject bytes but cannot replace the current workflow, its discriminator, or the tests that confer evidence authority. The two verified Git roots must be disjoint.

Before any dependency or build process runs, the action freezes path membership from each expected commit tree and creates an independent filesystem manifest over the actual checkout. It binds each tracked entry's raw name, lstat type, Unix mode, byte length, hard-link count, and SHA-256 content (or exact symbolic-link target), plus every directory and its mode. The subject manifest additionally closes the complete non-`.git` filesystem inventory, including empty-directory presence. Source manifests stop at 100,000 leaves, 500,000 directories, 600,000 total visited nodes, and 1 GB of logical bytes; the path parser and tree walk enforce those processing bounds while reading rather than only after allocation. Later checks consume that frozen manifest directly rather than asking a potentially changed Git index or repository configuration what should count. Generated runtime build output may appear outside the tracked set only during the build: once the source check passes, a second complete non-`.git` manifest freezes every generated executable, dependency, internal directory, and other runtime node, bounded to 500,000 leaves, 1,000,000 directories, 1,500,000 visited nodes, and 4 GB. Runtime links must resolve back inside that frozen non-Git tree. Tracked source bytes cannot change, the actual execution tree cannot drift after build, and `.jevyr` remains a separately closed authority subtree whose absent and explicitly empty states are distinct. The direct checks run after build, before startup, after daemon shutdown, before publication, and in the final always-run guard; Git commit/tree/index checks remain defense-in-depth diagnostics.

Subject capture reads `.jevyrignore` from the subject root, so the action rejects links and non-files there and requires the subject policy's presence and bytes to match the trusted base policy. A proposal that changes `.jevyrignore` cannot choose what Jevyr sees in its own run; it fails closed until that policy is independently reviewed and merged for later runs. The trusted runtime's entire `.jevyr` control namespace must be a real directory without symbolic links and remain free of modified, untracked, or ignored material after the dependency build, immediately before daemon startup, before publication, and at shutdown. Thus an installer or build cannot silently introduce or redirect a conventional policy, CLI configuration, or Assay Frontier outside the exact base commit.

It is intentionally advisory. Its token permission is read-only, it references no repository secret, and it cannot comment, push, merge, alter branch protection, or apply the Forge artifact. No package manager, host shell, local action, cache, or host build runs from the subject checkout. The trusted build requests and verifies exact Node 24.16.0 and pnpm 10.17.1 versions; their installers, generated executables, and the hosted runner remain external infrastructure trust. Runtime build, daemon, CLI, and export-verifier processes receive allowlisted empty environments with private HOME/TMPDIR, excluding Actions credentials and ambient provider keys; the daemon uses a dynamically assigned loopback port. After every prepublication invariant succeeds, the companion workflow uploads only a job summary plus one verified tar containing the signed Seal, Record, and terminal closure, immutable sealed Case, trust material, exact IntentContract and policy descriptor, Case-bound workflow/runtime/subject provenance, terminal status, complete terminal event ledger, verified content-addressed artifacts, the independent replay report, and a checked SHA-256 bundle manifest. The tar is extracted and verified before exposure, uploaded as the artifact's sole file, downloaded again, matched to the pre-upload archive digest, extracted again, and independently verified before the job can succeed. GitHub's artifact digest and Jevyr's inner archive digest are both written to the trusted job summary. The canonical provenance bytes are sealed as the sole second text subject; the export verifies their raw digest against that signed Case. The terminal receipt independently signs the exact final status projection, ledger head and sequence, canonical Record digest, and canonical artifact-index digest with the same key as the Seal and Record. Every exported artifact body is then checked against that authenticated index. Unstructured daemon/CLI/watch logs and the signing key remain in the disjoint private state directory. A rejected or unproven Record does not itself fail the workflow; authenticity, replay integrity, source or runtime mutation, recognizable credential material, publication mismatch, or infrastructure failure does.

The pinned checkout action's `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout` acknowledgement is set only for fetching fork bytes into the subject directory. LFS, submodule initialization, credential persistence, and global `safe.directory` mutation are disabled; a mode-`160000` gitlink in either frozen tree is rejected explicitly because its referenced content is absent and therefore cannot be sealed. The fetched checkout is never used as host executable input.

The companion workflow is still advisory source inside the repository. `pull_request_target` makes the workflow definition come from the base repository's default branch, so the PR under judgment cannot rewrite its own run. The workflow rejects pull requests aimed at any other base branch and manual dispatches from any other ref; treating that branch as executable authority requires the repository default branch itself to be protected and reviewed. A separately reviewed workflow change can still alter future runs after it merges; this is not an external repository-policy anchor. A required decision must pin Jevyr outside the subject repository—for example through an organization ruleset/required workflow, a GitHub App/external verifier, or a base-owned handoff that runs on a separate trusted runner—and authenticate that external trust root.

The per-run trust bundle proves internal DSSE consistency but is not an external identity anchor. `MANIFEST.sha256` is a corruption checksum, not a signature. Before Cast, the action privately commits the exact normalized impulse/submission/intent and expected clean Git snapshot; the sealed Case must match those expectations before export, and its IntentContract must equal a fresh compilation from that intent. Before publishing, the action runs the offline `verify-bundle` path over the finalized directory with the just-verified key ID and exact workflow/runtime/subject SHAs; this independently replays only the exported bytes and requires the terminal receipt to close the full post-Record tail. The action exposes the verified `key-id` output and prints it beside those SHAs in the trusted job summary. Later offline use must repeat that validation with the expected key ID or an artifact digest obtained from the authenticated GitHub run, or a separately pinned trust root; it must not trust the replay report or manifest alone.

Embodiment authority is optional but explicit. `assay-frontier` names a complete `jevyr.assay-frontier/1` file and `forge-plan` names the legacy single-plan form; the action rejects configuring both. Only relative, regular files tracked by and contained in the verified runtime commit are accepted. Private-state and public-export overrides must name new, disjoint directories below `RUNNER_TEMP`, so an output path cannot alias either checkout, stale proof, or private state.
